From 69ea463021be0d159ab30f96195fb0dd18ee2272 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Guo Ren <guoren@linux.alibaba.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2021 17:47:48 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] irqchip/sifive-plic: Fixup EOI failed when masked

When using "devm_request_threaded_irq(,,,,IRQF_ONESHOT,,)" in a driver,
only the first interrupt is handled, and following interrupts are never
delivered (initially reported in [1]).

That's because the RISC-V PLIC cannot EOI masked interrupts, as explained
in the description of Interrupt Completion in the PLIC spec [2]:

<quote>
The PLIC signals it has completed executing an interrupt handler by
writing the interrupt ID it received from the claim to the claim/complete
register. The PLIC does not check whether the completion ID is the same
as the last claim ID for that target. If the completion ID does not match
an interrupt source that *is currently enabled* for the target, the
completion is silently ignored.
</quote>

Re-enable the interrupt before completion if it has been masked during
the handling, and remask it afterwards.

[1] http://lists.infradead.org/pipermail/linux-riscv/2021-July/007441.html
[2] https://github.com/riscv/riscv-plic-spec/blob/8bc15a35d07c9edf7b5d23fec9728302595ffc4d/riscv-plic.adoc

Fixes: bb0fed1c60cc ("irqchip/sifive-plic: Switch to fasteoi flow")
Reported-by: Vincent Pelletier <plr.vincent@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Nikita Shubin <nikita.shubin@maquefel.me>
Signed-off-by: Guo Ren <guoren@linux.alibaba.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@dabbelt.com>
Cc: Atish Patra <atish.patra@wdc.com>

diff --git a/drivers/irqchip/irq-sifive-plic.c b/drivers/irqchip/irq-sifive-plic.c
index cf74cfa82045..259065d271ef 100644
--- a/drivers/irqchip/irq-sifive-plic.c
+++ b/drivers/irqchip/irq-sifive-plic.c
@@ -163,7 +163,13 @@ static void plic_irq_eoi(struct irq_data *d)
 {
 	struct plic_handler *handler = this_cpu_ptr(&plic_handlers);
 
-	writel(d->hwirq, handler->hart_base + CONTEXT_CLAIM);
+	if (irqd_irq_masked(d)) {
+		plic_irq_unmask(d);
+		writel(d->hwirq, handler->hart_base + CONTEXT_CLAIM);
+		plic_irq_mask(d);
+	} else {
+		writel(d->hwirq, handler->hart_base + CONTEXT_CLAIM);
+	}
 }
 
 static struct irq_chip plic_chip = {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/irqchip/irq-sifive-plic.c`**
- The function `plic_irq_eoi` was modified to handle the End of Interrupt (EOI) process differently when the interrupt is masked.
- If the interrupt is masked (`irqd_irq_masked(d)`), the interrupt is first unmasked using `plic_irq_unmask(d)`, then the EOI is acknowledged by writing to the `CONTEXT_CLAIM` register, and finally, the interrupt is masked again using `plic_irq_mask(d)`.
- If the interrupt is not masked, the EOI is acknowledged directly without any changes to the interrupt mask.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The changes in the `plic_irq_eoi` function address a specific issue where masked interrupts were not being properly acknowledged, leading to only the first interrupt being handled when using `devm_request_threaded_irq` with the `IRQF_ONESHOT` flag.
- By ensuring that masked interrupts are unmasked before acknowledging the EOI and then remasked, the patch fixes the bug reported by Vincent Pelletier, thus improving the interrupt handling mechanism in the RISC-V PLIC driver. This modification is directly related to the previously reported issue and is a corrective measure to ensure proper functionality of the interrupt handling in the driver.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the RISC-V PLIC does not allow for the End of Interrupt (EOI) to be acknowledged for masked interrupts. When an interrupt is masked during handling, the EOI signal is ignored, leading to subsequent interrupts not being delivered. This behavior violates the expected functionality when using `devm_request_threaded_irq` with the `IRQF_ONESHOT` flag, resulting in only the first interrupt being processed.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void plic_irq_eoi(struct irq_data *d)
 {
 	struct plic_handler *handler = this_cpu_ptr(&plic_handlers);
 
-	writel(d->hwirq, handler->hart_base + CONTEXT_CLAIM);
+	if (irqd_irq_masked(d)) {
+		plic_irq_unmask(d);
+		writel(d->hwirq, handler->hart_base + CONTEXT_CLAIM);
+		plic_irq_mask(d);
+	} else {
+		writel(d->hwirq, handler->hart_base + CONTEXT_CLAIM);
+	}
 }

When an interrupt is masked (checked by `irqd_irq_masked(d)`), the EOI signal (via `writel(d->hwirq, handler->hart_base + CONTEXT_CLAIM)`) is ignored, preventing subsequent interrupts from being delivered.

The fix involves unmasking the interrupt before sending the EOI signal (`plic_irq_unmask(d)`) to ensure that the EOI is acknowledged correctly.
